name: Shrewsbury cast-iron framed flax mill
description: A five-storey flax mill used cast-iron columns and beams with brick floor arches and wrought-iron ties, an industrial framing system designed to limit fire damage.

impact.note: One mill made safer from fire by an iron frame; a handful of iron-framed mills followed directly, though later framed buildings had many sources.

date.basis: The cited source reports this year for the scoped event.

events.statement: The Shrewsbury Main Mill opened as a flax-spinning mill with its iron-framed structure.

evidence.locator: A pioneering design; flax mill years
evidence.supports: The Shrewsbury Main Mill opened as a flax-spinning mill with its iron-framed structure.
Hazledine’s foundry supplied the frame castings.

contributions.group: Thomas and Benjamin Benyon with John Marshall
contributions.resource: Commissioned and operated the new flax mill

evidence.supports: The partners chose the site and engaged Bage to build the mill.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest sourced date for the specific documented case; this does not establish invention or worldwide priority.

caveats: The source is an institutional historical synthesis; it does not establish the absence of earlier iron-framed constructions worldwide.

research.note: Independently checked 1797 opening, five-storey design and cast-iron supplier against Historic England. Charles Bage was the designer, but his contribution awaits a registered person rather than a group entry.

evidence.supports: The Main Mill had five storeys.
